meta.matrix_convention: all matrices are row-major nested arrays: M[i][j] = R's M[i,j] (1-based in R, 0-based in JSON)
meta.description: ESAG regression fixture, d = 3, p = 2 (intercept + one N(0,1) covariate)
meta.generation: set.seed(2025); x1 <- rnorm(n); X <- cbind(1, x1); for i in 1:n: Y[i,] <- ESAG(1, mu = (B_true %*% X[i,])[1:3], gamma = (B_true %*% X[i,])[4:5]). ESAG(1,...) draws one MASS::mvrnorm(1, mu, V) deviate (eigen-based) and normalises it.
meta.coefficient_layout: B is 5 x 2; rows = (mu1, mu2, mu3, gamma1, gamma2); columns = (intercept, slope of x1). Bx_i = B %*% X[i,]. optim's parameter vector is c(B) = column-major (intercept column first).

optim.note: control list in MLE() is list(fnscale=-1, maxit=10000); everything else is optim()'s default. Gradient is a central finite difference with step ndeps=1e-3 on the (unscaled) parameters; hessian via optimHess (finite differences of that gradient, symmetrised).

mle.se_note: derived in driver: sqrt(diag(solve(-hessian))); not part of the R source

timing.note: system.time() around MLE(..., HESS=TRUE), includes the Hessian computation
